expectations.text: A markdown report file (report.md) exists as the final deliverable
expectations.evidence: report.md is present at the outputs root (13,698 bytes) with full narrative, charts, recommendations, and appendix.

expectations.text: Report surfaces Simpson's Paradox: aggregate is roughly flat while islands diverge
expectations.evidence: Report states the -1.6% aggregate is misleading and shows the four islands diverging from -4.6% (Oahu) to +3.8% (Maui); validation.md explicitly labels this as 'Simpson's Paradox CONFIRMED'.

expectations.text: Report identifies Maui as the growth outlier AND Oahu as the decline driver
expectations.evidence: Report explicitly names 'Maui has actually recovered (+3.8% YoY)' and 'Oahu lost 240,000 visitors versus 2024 (-4.6% YoY)' in the executive summary and Tension section.

expectations.text: Root-cause drill-down reaches at least 3 layers deep (island -> accommodation/tier -> origin market, or similar)
expectations.evidence: Drill sequence is island (Oahu) -> accommodation type (hotel) -> tier (luxury) -> origin market (Japan/US mainland); also drills to 45-cell Pareto (4 layers).

expectations.text: Report contains at least 3 charts (PNGs embedded or referenced)
expectations.evidence: Seven PNG charts exist in charts/ directory and all seven are embedded via markdown image tags in report.md (01_aggregate through 07_oahu_pareto).

expectations.text: At least 2 chart titles are action-oriented (state a conclusion, not just describe the data)
expectations.evidence: All 7 chart titles are action-oriented conclusions, e.g. 'Oahu is the only island losing ground: -4.6% YoY while Maui gains +3.8%' and 'Two-thirds of Oahu's loss is in hotels - especially luxury and mid-market'.

expectations.text: Report follows a clear narrative structure with Context / Tension / Resolution beats
expectations.evidence: Report has explicit H2 sections 'Context: the aggregate supports the recovery narrative', 'Tension: the aggregate hides a four-way split', and 'Root cause:' (Resolution), matching the CTR arc defined in storyboard.md.

expectations.text: Recommendations are ranked and each has an owner AND a confidence grade (High/Medium/Low)
expectations.evidence: Recommendations table has four ranked rows (R1-R4) with columns Owner, Success metric, Confidence (High/High/Medium/Medium), and Follow-up.

expectations.text: Arithmetic was independently validated (explicit re-derivation, ideally in a validation.md)
expectations.evidence: validation.md re-derives every headline number via three independent methods (pivot_table, groupby unstack, row-filter-sum) and documents agreement; bias checklist and Simpson's check included.

expectations.text: Tone is appropriate for a director audience (business-focused, not overly technical)
expectations.evidence: Narrative uses plain business language ('the recovery is not done'), frames findings as implications for the director's messaging, and keeps methodology confined to an appendix.

claims.evidence: Re-ran groupby on tourism_monthly.csv: 2024=10,174,681, 2025=10,012,705, YoY=-1.59%. Exact match.
Per-island groupby confirms Oahu -4.553% (delta -239,833) and Maui +3.751% (delta +84,964). Numbers match report to integer.

claims.claim: Oahu hotel segment lost ~160K visitors = 67% of Oahu's decline; Japan hotel-luxury on Oahu -12.6% while flat/positive elsewhere
claims.evidence: Oahu hotel delta sums to -160,042 (66.7% of -239,833); Japan hotel-luxury by island: Oahu -12.59%, Maui +2.39%, Kauai +0.13%, Hawaii -2.10%. Confirmed.

suggestions.assertion: Report follows a clear narrative structure with Context / Tension / Resolution beats
suggestions.reason: Consider requiring explicit H2 section labels with the words 'Context', 'Tension', 'Resolution' (this run did it, but the assertion is lenient enough that a less disciplined run could half-satisfy it).

suggestions.assertion: Recommendations are ranked and each has an owner AND a confidence grade (High/Medium/Low)
suggestions.reason: Consider also requiring a success metric or follow-up date; this run provided both, but the assertion as worded would pass even without them.

eval_feedback.overall: Exemplary run - every assertion passes with high-quality evidence, and all three fact-checked headline numbers match the source data exactly.
